title: Stacked pull requests: rebase the bottom without orphaning the top
summary: Three dependent branches stacked on each other. Rebase the bottom one onto main and watch the stack fall apart — then do it again with --update-refs, which fixes the whole stack in one pass.
mental_model: Each branch in a stack points at a specific commit. Rebasing the bottom branch creates new commits, so the branches above still point at the *old* ones. `--update-refs` moves every branch pointer that was inside the rebased range.

steps.title: See the stack
steps.why: Three branches, each one commit on top of the last. This is how large changes get reviewed in pieces — and it is fragile in exactly one way, which the next step demonstrates.
steps.expect: A single line of commits with three branch labels at different points.

steps.title: Rebase the bottom branch the naive way
steps.why: main moved, so feature/1-model needs rebasing. This works — but watch what it does to the two branches sitting above it.
steps.expect: feature/1-model moves onto main. The other two are still hanging off the OLD commit.

steps.title: See the damage
steps.why: feature/2-api and feature/3-ui now point at commits whose parent is the pre-rebase model commit. The stack has forked: rebasing them individually now means resolving the same conflicts once per branch.
steps.expect: feature/3-ui is three commits from main, and the model commit appears twice in the graph — once rebased, once not.

verify.label: the upper branches still carry the old, unrebased commits

steps.title: Undo it and start over
steps.why: `reset --hard ORIG_HEAD` puts the bottom branch back, restoring the stack. Now the whole thing can be done properly in a single command.

steps.title: Rebase the whole stack at once
steps.why: Run the rebase from the TOP branch with `--update-refs`. Git replays all three commits and moves every branch pointer that was inside the range — the entire stack lands on main, correctly ordered.
steps.expect: All three branches now sit on top of main, each still one commit apart.

verify.label: the bottom branch is one commit above main
the top branch is three commits above main, stack intact

steps.title: Confirm the stack is still a stack
steps.why: Each branch should contain exactly one more commit than the one below it. If that holds, every pull request in the stack still shows a one-commit diff.

verify.label: each branch is exactly one commit above the previous

steps.title: Make it automatic
steps.why: `rebase.updateRefs true` applies it to every rebase. If you work in stacks at all, this is the single most valuable git config line of the last few years.

verify.label: the bottom of the stack sits directly on main
verify.hint: git rebase --update-refs main, run from the top branch

verify.label: the middle branch is one commit above the bottom
the top branch is one commit above the middle
the whole stack rebased as a unit, nothing orphaned
the config is set so this never has to be remembered

pitfalls: `--update-refs` only moves branches whose tips are inside the rebased range. A branch pointing at a commit outside it is left alone, correctly.
Force-pushing a rebased stack must be done for every branch, and `--force-with-lease` is essential — each one has a stale remote counterpart.
Merging the bottom pull request first, then rebasing, is the usual workflow. Merging the top one first leaves the others describing changes that are already in.
Without `--update-refs` you can still fix a broken stack: rebase each branch with `--onto`, bottom-up. It just costs one conflict resolution per branch.
cheatsheet: rebase and move every branch in the range
see where every branch tip actually is
confirm each stack level is one commit
